links.targetTitle: Aligned Delegates currently serve as the primary Ecosystem S

title: Aligned Delegate recognition proves control of two Ethereum addresses without revealing any identity
content:
A.1.6.1.3 makes recognition as an Aligned Delegate conditional on completing a specific cryptographic ritual rather than on any disclosure. The applicant must first deploy at least one Delegate Contract (A.1.6.1.3.1), then post a public AD Recognition Submission Message on the Sky Forum (A.1.6.1.3.2) containing links to **two** signed messages:

- One signed by "the applicant's Ethereum address controlling the deployed Delegate Contract(s)," which "demonstrates that the applicant controls the Ethereum address that, in turn, controls their deployed Delegate Contract(s)" (A.1.6.1.3.2.1).
- One signed by "the applicant's Ecosystem Actor Ethereum address" (A.1.6.1.3.2.2).

Each must carry a prescribed title and "a timestamp recording the time and date that the message was cryptographically signed," and A.1.6.1.3.3 fixes the exact forum template.

The design is a neat resolution of an apparent contradiction in the AC regime. Delegates hold real voting power and must be accountable, yet A.1.5.7 requires them to be anonymous. Signature-based proof satisfies both: it establishes that one actor controls both the delegation contract and the ecosystem identity, binding the pseudonym to verifiable on-chain facts, while revealing nothing about who they are.

The two-signature requirement is what makes it more than an address check — it links a *governance* identity to a *payment/actor* identity, so a delegate cannot separate the reputation attached to their forum presence from the addresses that receive delegation and funds. Timestamps prevent replay of an old signature, and the mandatory titles make each signature specific to this purpose rather than reusable.

A.1.6.1.3.2.0.3.1 points to Etherscan's Verified Signature mechanism as the practical route, showing the process is intentionally executable with public tooling and no privileged infrastructure.
description: A.1.6.1.3 requires a deployed Delegate Contract plus two cryptographically signed forum messages
